key_insight: PISA is a preconditioned inexact stochastic ADMM optimizer that enables stable, provably convergent training of deep models under minimal assumptions, while handling heterogeneous data and a variety of preconditioners. It matches or outperforms standard optimizers across diverse tasks.
problem_solved: Training deep models when data is heterogeneous, problems are ill-conditioned, or only inexact/local updates are feasible—situations where existing optimizers lack robustness, flexibility, or strong convergence guarantees.
method: Formulate a preconditioned, stochastic ADMM framework that permits inexact (approximate) subproblem solves and flexible preconditioners (diagonal, block, quasi-Newton, etc.).
Use stochastic updates that accommodate heterogeneous data across nodes/partitions while retaining a global coordination step via ADMM.
Provide theoretical convergence guarantees under minimal assumptions and demonstrate empirical gains over common optimizers on multiple tasks.
impact: Gives practitioners a robust, flexible optimizer for distributed/federated and ill-conditioned training scenarios, reducing tuning and improving stability and performance for real-world heterogeneous datasets.
visual_elements: Flow diagram of PISA: local stochastic/inexact update → preconditioning → ADMM coordination step
Convergence plots comparing PISA vs. Adam/SGD/ADMM variants on accuracy and loss across tasks
Schematic showing heterogeneous nodes/data partitions and interchangeable preconditioner icons (diagonal, block, quasi-Newton)
Callout box listing minimal assumptions and a simple badge/icon indicating “provable convergence”
paper_title: Preconditioned inexact stochastic ADMM for deep models
paper_authors: Shenglong Zhou, Ouya Wang, Ziyan Luo, Yongxu Zhu, Geoffrey Ye Li
